subject: Re: Structuring a multi-tier 'Usage Insurance' discount and channel split for GCP Private Offer
messages:
From: Emma Parker <emma.parker@skylinehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@skylinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Usage insurance / channel split proposal question

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked Redwood's latency profile. We're moving toward a GCP private offer for the next 12 months and Procurement asked me to check one structural ask before we move to legal.

We expect bursty usage from our telemetry pipeline and want to avoid big overage surprises. Our cloud team proposed a multi-tier "Usage Insurance" discount that kicks in as usage exceeds forecast bands. The structure would offer: 5% discount for +10% over forecast, 12% for +25% and 20% for +50% (applied retroactively to baseline tokens).

Two questions for Redwood:
- Can this be expressed inside a GCP private offer and still allow standard marketplace invoicing?
- How do you typically handle channel splits / reseller commissions when discounts are retroactive? Procurement prefers the reseller to not be penalized for our overage protection.

I've attached our baseline usage spreadsheet and a draft of the PO terms. Happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Best,
Emma Parker
Head of Cloud Procurement
Skyline Health
Attachment: Skyline_GCP_Usage_Baseline.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: Draft_PO_Terms_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Emma Parker <emma.parker@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage insurance / channel split proposal question

Emma — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments. Quick answers up front: yes, we can encode banded, retroactive discounts into a GCP private offer (it will be a custom pricing schedule) and yes, we can preserve a reseller/partner commission path so partners are not shorted when discounts apply retroactively.

I'll capture the recommended approach below and loop Ben (channel ops) and Rishi (pricing/contracts) for implementation details. Proposed approach:

- Encode the banded thresholds as pricing tiers within the Private Offer. Each tier is associated with a discount flag and an effective retroactive application window for the quarter.
- Keep the marketplace invoice semantics intact by using a blended invoice line item: list price charged by GCP, Redwood issues a credit memo reflecting the retro discount applied to the baseline once usage is reconciled.
- The reseller commission is calculated on the net revenue after Redwood credits are applied; Redwood will issue matching uplift credits to the reseller so they're not penalized. Alternatively, we can create a protected partner fee that is paid based on a pre-discount baseline (preferred if reseller contract requires guaranteed margin).

Ben/Rishi: can you confirm operational feasibility and which option (reseller credit vs. protected fee) is simpler from an ops and tax perspective?

Next steps: if we agree, I'll draft a short mutual action plan and a reconciled invoice example for Procurement to review. Happy to take a call Thursday afternoon.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Partnerships (Marketplace)
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage insurance / channel split proposal question

Looping in the ops view. Quick operational notes:

- GCP Private Offers support tiered pricing, but the marketplace will still invoice at list. That means we need a clean post-invoice credit flow. We have two tested options: (A) Redwood issues a single quarterly credit memo to Skyline and a matching commission adjustment to the reseller (clean, but requires credit memo cadence alignment); (B) Redwood keeps a partner-protected commission line on our side and pays the reseller the pre-discount commission (simpler for partner P&L but slightly more complex from revenue recognition).

- Taxes and reseller treatment: Option B is preferable when partners insist on guaranteed margin (less frequent partner disputes). Option A is simpler for bookkeeping when discounts are rare or immaterial.

- Implementation detail: we can automate reconciliation if Skyline provides a token-usage feed or grants limited read-only access to the usage report. Attached is a sample reconciliation table (we'll generate a signed PDF post-quarter).

Suggested default for this deal: Option B (protected partner fee) for first year, then migrate to Option A if both parties are comfortable after two reconciliations.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Channel Operations
Attachment: sample_reconciliation_table.pdf (pdf)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, Emma Parker <emma.parker@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage insurance / channel split proposal question

Emma — following the internal discussion, a few legal/contract points to note before we finalize language:

1) Wording on retroactive discounts: we'll reference a "Usage Reconciliation Credit" which is applied within 60 days after the quarter close. The credit will be calculated against the baseline token subset defined in the PO.
2) Partner protection clause: for this deal we'll include a "Partner Margin Preservation" clause that guarantees the partner commission rate on the pre-discount baseline for the first 12 months. This means Redwood will pay the reseller based on list price for settlement periods and absorb the crediting delta internally.

3) Audit and evidence: Skyline will need to provide token usage reports (CSV or GCP billing export) for the reconciliation. We can accept signed exports from your cloud team or grant read-only billing access.

4) Invoice example: we will produce a specimen invoice + credit memo flow and include it as Annex A to the PO so Procurement can see mechanics before Legal signs off.

If that sounds good, Lauren — I'll prepare a short PO amendment (1 page) with these bullet points and circulation to Skyline's procurement/legal. Emma — can you confirm whether Procurement wants the protected partner fee (Option B) for the entire 12 months? If yes we'll bake that in and flag the revenue recognition note for Finance.

Thanks — cc'ing Ben for ops handoff.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
